speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; to help me determine the cause, please tell me if this sensation involves the entire room spinning or just a sense of imbalance, and how long each episode lasts. Also, have you experienced any nausea, vomiting, or hearing changes like ringing in the ears or muffled hearing alongside the dizziness?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

The presentation of brief, spontaneous vertigo episodes lasting under a minute, accompanied by nausea/vomiting, is classic for BPPV. Since you are currently at baseline and the episode was isolated, no further testing is required at this time.
